info.bio:
Rollins Band es el proyecto musical de Henry Rollins y con el que se ha mantenido más tiempo en activo. A través de esta agrupación Rollins entrega un mensaje critico de introspección, a veces vehemente y otras veces repleto de humor negro.

Una primera encarnación de la banda (bajo el nombre Henrietta Collins & the Wife-Beating Child Haters) edita con Henry Rollins el álbum Hot Animal Machine entregando un sonido basado en el post-punk pero con reminiscencias al heavy metal y el jazz.

scenes.name: Cruces del punk: de Fugazi al punk-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el punk es el más vivo de los subgéneros del rock: miles de bandas ensayando en garajes, un lenguaje universal como no se veía desde los sesenta. Nueva York: Adrenalin O.D., el straight-edge de Youth Of Today y Gorilla Biscuits, el crossover punk-metal (Cro-Mags, Prong, Danzig). Washington lanza a Pussy Galore (la irrelevancia hecha relevante), Unrest y Fugazi de Ian MacKaye, que abstrae el hardcore en una forma teatral de compromiso ético y estético (Repeater, Steady Diet Of Nothing, Red Medicine), y Royal Trux (Twin Infinitives, «un Trout Mask Replica para la generación grunge»). El punk-pop de Mr T Experience, Dwarves, Henry Rollins, L7 (pioneras del «foxcore»), Lemonheads, Screeching Weasel, Goo Goo Dolls, Fastbacks, Shonen Knife; el «rogue folk» de los Pogues, Membranes y Chumbawamba.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
podcast.body: Rollins Band was part of the inaugural Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, a successful event that showcased the growing audience for alternative music and prompted promoters to establish it as an annual festival. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza Performance (1991)
podcast.body: The Rollins Band was featured on the lineup of the inaugural Lollapalooza tour, which sought to combine various up-and-coming alternative bands to fill larger venues. "It featured Jane's Addiction as the headliners along with up and coming bands like Nine Inch Nails and the Rollins Band along with Ice Tea and Body Counts and the Butthole Surfers and Suzy and the Banshees and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Co-headlining Tour with Beastie Boys
podcast.body: The Rollins Band toured alongside the Beastie Boys after the release of *Check Your Head*, highlighting the Beastie Boys' eclectic touring partners. "They toured not only with Cypress Hill, but also get this, The Rollins Band."

xref.title: Development and Opening Slots
xref.body: Mighty Joe Young spent about two years playing numerous gigs to develop their sound and performance skills, eventually drawing audiences of a couple hundred people on their own. This success led to opening slots for bands such as Solar Sylem and the Rollins Band. "This band worked out their chops by playing gig after gig for about two years, eventually drawing a couple hundred people on their own which led to opening slots for bands like Solar Sylem and the Rollins band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Genre Blending and Influence
xref.body: NoMeansNo occupied a unique space by blending elements of hardcore and metal. Their sound contained elements that would later define post-hardcore, influencing bands like At the Drive-In, Rollins Band, Alexisonfire, Billy Talent, Deftones, and Silverstein. "They ended up occupying a space somewhere between hardcore and metal. If you listen carefully to what they did, you can hear elements of what would become known as post-hardcore, a sound that would later birth groups like at the drive-in, Rollins Band, Alexis on Fire, Billy Talent, The Death Tones and Silverstein."
